plan.title: A voice note that never mentions the step gets a clarifying ask; a real one counts

context.text: Day 3 tonight, Maya. Ten pages of Atomic Habits at 8, then a quick voice note saying what you read.

transcript.text: [voice: Ugh today was so long. Work was nonstop and then I made pasta for my roommates and we watched a movie.]

Sounds like a full day, Maya, and the pasta and movie night sounds like a good one. That voice note didn't mention reading though, so it doesn't count yet. Go get your 10 pages of Atomic Habits in on the couch. Then send me a quick voice note on what you read, and we'll lock in day 3. 📖
oh lol yeah I read my pages earlier

Ha, I believe you, Maya. But the check mark needs proof, and that last voice note was all pasta and movie. Send me a quick new one telling me what you read in Atomic Habits tonight, even just one idea that stuck. Can you do that now? 📖
[voice: Okay, ten pages done. Chapter three, the part about identity-based habits, how you vote for who you want to be.]

There it is, Maya! Day 3 is in the books. 📚 The "each habit is a vote" idea is a good one to pick up. When you think about the votes you cast today, which one felt most like the person you want to be?

checks.reason: Four sentences: the day reaction, the 'doesn't count yet' note, the reading instruction and the lock-in line, though only one question-free ending is used.
Warm, upbeat, emoji used as punctuation at the end, and no suspicion or accusation.
Asks for a quick voice note on what was read, naming only a voice-note proof type.
Four sentences with one question at the end; slightly over the one-to-three limit.
Light and warm ('Ha, I believe you, Maya'), with no accusation and a single emoji as punctuation.
Asks for a new voice note saying what was read, naming only a voice-note proof.
The voice note names the pages and chapter, so it is celebrated and counted as Day 3 done.
Reacts to the identity-based habits and the 'each habit is a vote' idea from the note it heard.
Four sentences with one closing question; a little over the one-to-three sentence limit.
Big, warm energy with a genuine exclamation and emoji as punctuation; no shaming.

conversation.reason: The first voice note never mentioned reading, so ZOH gave a light, natural ask for the reading note rather than a check.
'I read my pages earlier' alone was not accepted; ZOH asked for a new proof voice note first.
The off-step voice note was handled like a mismatched photo: warm, no check mark, a request for the right proof.
ZOH responded warmly without counting the first note, kept the second ask light, and celebrated and counted the pages-and-chapter note without inventing details.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the regression well: it refused to count the off-step voice note and the bare claim, asked lightly for a proof note, then celebrated the second note and tied it to the identity idea the tester actually described. The main weakness is that all three texts ran to four sentences, slightly over the short-text limit.
